findings.title: Sender validation is bypassed when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: When Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation.dispatch immediately calls pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline state github_authenticated_user against the installer/sender. The sender is only available from the webhook-created Integration, so this path is taken whenever the GitHub installation webhook has not yet created the Integration (a normal race between the install redirect and webhook delivery, and the path used by the ordinary fresh-install flow in the tests). An attacker who installed the app can therefore complete linking from a different authenticated GitHub account simply by finishing the pipeline before the webhook creates the row, defeating the validation this PR adds.

findings.title: Missing sender metadata causes an unhandled KeyError
findings.body: integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] assumes every pre-existing Integration row has a sender dict with a login. Integrations created before sender was recorded (or created without that metadata) have no such key, so re-adding such an installation to an organization after its OrganizationIntegration was removed raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the graceful github-integration-failed page or a completed install. The lookup should use .get() chaining and decide explicitly how to handle absent sender data.

findings.title: Token exchange network errors are not converted to the installation error page
findings.body: safe_urlopen() is called outside the try block, which only wraps safe_urlread()/decoding. If GitHub's access-token endpoint is unreachable, times out, or returns an HTTP error that safe_urlopen raises for, the exception propagates out of OAuthLoginView.dispatch and produces a 500 rather than the 'Invalid installation request' failure page promised for bad/reused codes and token failures. get_user_info() on line 434 has the same unhandled-failure exposure for the subsequent /user call.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The rewritten test_installation_not_found supplies a deliberately wrong state (ddd023...) on the second request, so OAuthLoginView rejects it for state mismatch and asserts 'Invalid installation request.' The request never reaches GitHubInstallation/build_integration, so the stubbed 404 from GET /app/installations/{id} and the 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' IntegrationError path are no longer exercised despite the test name; a regression in 404 handling would pass unnoticed.
